newsitem.title: USA: Royal Standard Mineral says assessment done.
newsitem.headline: Royal Standard Mineral says assessment done.

text.p: Royal Standard Mineral said Monday a preliminary assessment of the economic viability of the South Bullion deposit in Nevada has been completed, showing about 80,000 ounces of recoverable gold and about 363,000 ounces of recoverable silver.
The company said preliminary studies by Bharti Engineering Associates indicate the project could be made profitable and should proceed to the next stage of development.

Based on more than 200 closely-spaced reverse circulation drill holes, diluted bulk mineable reserves were determined to be 3.9 million tons grading 0.027 opt gold and 0.198 opt silver, the company said.

Using 75 percent silver and 50 percent gold recoveries, and a 1.27:1.0 waste-to-strip ratio, the currently identified deposit hosts about 80,000 ounces of recoverable gold and 363,000 ounces of recoverable silver, the company said.
The deposit is located in the Carlin Trend, about 10 miles south of Newmount's Rain gold mine in Elko County, Nev.
Royal Standard holds a 70 percent operating interest in the project. The remaining 30 percent is held by its partner, Crown Resources Corp.

A first-round 5,000 foot diamond drilling program is expected to begin in late September. Based on the study, the company said it believes that a two-fold or better increase in the reserves can be achieved by the drilling program.
Drill testing of several deep, high-grade "feeder" targets adjacent to the identified reserves has been postponed until the drilling program is completed, the company said.
